label: Cavazos-Rehg et al. 2014 — Google Trends cigar searches vs youth cigar use by state (faithful)
_locked_note: v2 replaces v1 (commit aa7e2ea) before any Google Trends value was seen: v1 could not be sent (see _v2_change). A change produces a new preset version.
_why_provider_params: The paper limits results to the United States and to 2011 and maps states; include_low_search_volume keeps low-volume states as values (2011 Trends showed them as 0) instead of dropping them.

queries._source: PMC4122644, Methods, 'Google Trends data'. The paper's 15 terms, reduced to the 8 whose words every paper term contains (see _v2_change), joined with Google Trends' + (OR) operator in one query.

comparisons.label: RSV „cigar” (2011) vs odsetek uczniów palących cygara (YRBS 2011)

_v2_change.why: SerpApi refuses a Google Trends query longer than 100 characters (HTTP 400, run 7aa42db5 on a test copy; no value was returned). The paper's 15 terms joined with ' + ' are about 220 characters.
_v2_change.equivalence: Without quotes, Google Trends matches searches that contain all words of a term. Every paper term contains all words of one of the 8 kept terms (little/flavored/Phillies/sweet/JR/Dutch Master/White Owl cigars -> cigars), so the OR of the 8 covers the same searches as the OR of the 15. This is an argument from Trends' documented matching, not a measurement.
_v2_change.joiner: '+' without spaces (93 characters). Checked on neutral terms before any cigar request: 'tennis+squash' and 'tennis + squash' (US, 2011, by region) returned identical values for all 51 regions (docs/history/evidence/2026-10-26-cr2014/plus_check/).
